newsitem.title: UK: Russia bought a quarter of Cuba's Q1 sugar exports.
newsitem.headline: Russia bought a quarter of Cuba's Q1 sugar exports.

text.p: Russia took more than a quarter of Cuba's first quarter sugar exports in 1997, importing over half a million tonnes of raws, the International Sugar Organization (ISO) said on Wednesday.

Russia imported 534,402 tonnes of the total 1.86 million tonnes exported by Cuba in the cumulative January/March period. Cuba exported 2.17 million tonnes of sugar, all raw, in the same period a year ago.
But Russia's imports of Cuban raws were sharply lower than last year when they totalled 1.23 million tonnes, ISO data showed.

Russia took the lion's share of Cuban sugar exports for March alone, importing 253,580 tonnes -- way ahead of other major buyers such as Egypt and China, which took 161,757 and 71,510 tonnes respectively.
Cumulatively, Egypt and China were also the biggest buyers after Russia for the first quarter, importing 276,523 and 212,073 tonnes and closely followed by Japan with 191,644 tonnes.
Egypt imported 40,402 tonnes in the first three months of 1996, China 142,020 but Japan imported nothing, ISO data showed.
